localChanges: In Civilization II games, the Civilopedia now also says what buildings and Wonders do against barbarians, in talks with other leaders, to trade routes, pollution and global warming, and what a city loses when it's conquered (closes #1291).

In Civilization II games, the Civilopedia also says how a Barracks' upkeep changes with the difficulty level and your advances, how Barracks help damaged units nearby, and what happens to your Palace when its city falls.

log: The barbarian attacker rule describes the Palace halving barbarian attacks in its city and the Great Wall halving them against all its owner's units; the barbarian defender rule describes the Great Wall's ×2 attack against barbarian defenders. Each number is now an exported constant the effect and its description both read.

The trade route income rule now describes the Airport (a route's link counts as at least 1 with one in both cities) and Superhighways (+1 to the link of this city's routes), reading constants lifted from lib/tradeRoutes.

Barracks say they're sold on Gunpowder and on Mobile Warfare, and what they cost below Prince and from Prince up at each stage. The Solar Plant says it counts against global warming and takes a step off its citizens' pollution. Captured cities say which improvements they lose, always or at even odds, and a new Palace says it moves the capital.

The Great Wall and the United Nations say that computer leaders accept their owner's peace, make it no aggressive demands and are warmer to it in talks; Marco Polo's that its computer owner asks more tribute; Marco Polo's and Magellan's that maps are shared without an alliance; and the Eiffel Tower that computer leaders hear more of its owner's proposals, that a broken treaty costs it a point less reputation, that its reputation recovers faster and that attitudes to it drift warmer.
The capture rule that splits an empire now describes it on the Palace: if the city with it is captured, its owner's empire may split in civil war. The conditions stay with the CivilWar rules.

The incite-revolt rule says a Courthouse makes the distance to the capital count half as much, the heal rule says Barracks heal land units within 3 squares 2 steps more, the allied-repair rule says Barracks repair an ally's units 2 tenths, and the Trireme loss rule says the Lighthouse keeps Triremes from being lost at sea. Each number is one exported constant the rule and its description read.

The Eiffel Tower says that its owner's reputation is halved, every other leader's attitude to it improves by 25 and every vendetta against it ends, when it is built or captured; the Manhattan Project that every civilization's reputation recovers halfway, to no worse than 6, when it is built.
